source.test: NeoForgeInstaller.listVersionPairs() / ForgeInstaller.parseMavenMetadata(_:) substring scrape on non-XML input

cases.raw_metadata_xml: this is not xml at all, just some text

cases.reason: no `<version>`/`</version>` substring pair is found by the scrape loop (lines 52-56), so `versions` ends up an empty array and `stable` (filtered from it) is also empty -- listVersionPairs then just returns an empty entries list, no throw

same mechanism -- parseMavenMetadata is a pure string scrape (line 418-425), never a real XML parser, so truncated/garbled markup that contains no complete <version>...</version> pair simply yields zero mavenVersions and an empty result

notes: The one genuinely surprising failure-shape result in this whole fixture set: garbled/non-XML input for the NeoForge/Forge metadata endpoints is NOT a parse error at the listVersionPairs level, because there is no real XML parser in this code path to fail -- both `NeoForgeInstaller.listVersionPairs` (lines 52-56) and `ForgeInstaller.parseMavenMetadata` (lines 418-425) hand-scan the raw text for literal `<version>`/`</version>` substring pairs via `range(of:)`, completely indifferent to whether the surrounding document is well-formed XML. Malformed input that happens to contain zero complete `<version>...</version>` pairs silently produces an empty version list, not a thrown error -- `provider-corpus-check.py`'s own `.xml` well-formedness check (which DOES use a real XML parser, `xml.etree.ElementTree`) exists purely to keep the *recorded evidence* honest; it says nothing about what MSC 1's own scrape would do if fed something malformed. The one place this DOES surface as a thrown error is one level up: `NeoForgeInstaller.latestStableVersion` (a different function, not this one) turns an empty `stable` array into `.noStableVersion` via its `guard let best = stable.max(...)`, already covered by empty-version-list-rejected-not-unified-across-providers. `listVersionPairs` itself never reaches that guard -- an empty entries array is a perfectly valid return value for the picker.
